title: Sweden vs Romania: Nations League debut and what to expect
seoTitle: Sweden vs Romania: Nations League debut
subtitle: Promoted teams in Group B4 set to define the opening steps of the competition
excerpt: Sweden and Romania face off this Friday, September 25, in the first round of the Nations League.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On the afternoon of September 25, the Strawberry Arena hosts the clash between Sweden and Romania, a match that opens the group stage of the UEFA Nations League 2026-27. The game gained prominence because both teams have just been promoted to League B and need a positive point to kick off the new campaign.

Reasons for high demand for the match

The encounter marks the first game for both sides in League B after earning promotion in the previous edition. The result could determine who leads Group B4 even at the opening round, which raises fan interest.

How the teams arrived at the showdown

Sweden earned promotion after winning its group in League C and also participated in the 2026 World Cup, where it was eliminated by France. In its last 21 matches, the Swedish side has five wins, 12 losses, and four draws, showing an uneven performance.

Romania, the leader of its group in the previous Nations League, lost in the European World Cup playoffs and played recent friendlies, including a win over Wales and a draw with Georgia. In 20 matches, Romania has six wins, 12 losses, and two draws.

Probable line‑ups and absences

For Sweden, the likely formation includes Viktor Johansson; Emil Holm, Victor Lindelöf, Carl Starfelt and Gabriel Gudmundsson; Lucas Bergvall, Mattias Svanberg, Yasin Ayari and Sebastian Nanasi; Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyökeres. Manager Jon Dahl Tomasson will not have Gustaf Lagerbielke available due to injury.

Romania should start with Ionuț Radu; Andrei Rațiu, Radu Drăgușin, Andrei Burcă and Nicușor Bancu; Răzvan Marin, Marius Marin and Nicolae Stanciu; Dennis Man, Denis Drăguș and Valentin Mihăilă. Coach Mircea Lucescu will miss Radu Drăgușin, who is sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament rupture.

Tactical expectations and decisive factors

The Swedes may opt for a 3-5-2, aiming to dictate tempo and use the attacking pair of Isak and Gyökeres. Romania, under Gheorghe Hagi, tends to play a 4-3-3, exploiting counter‑attacks and the width of the wingers. Midfield battle and offensive efficiency will be crucial, as both sides have shown vulnerable defenses in the last ten games.

Where to watch and market odds

No confirmed broadcast in Brazil; the match can be followed live via betting apps. Bookmakers set Sweden as the favorite (odds 1.40), draw at 4.50 and a Romanian win at 6.50. The goal market offers 1.50 for over 2.5 and 2.55 for under 2.5, with both teams scoring at 1.75.

With three points on the line, the Sweden‑Romania clash promises to be balanced and decisive for the start of the Nations League. The result could place one side at the top of Group B4 or open the way for a tight contest in upcoming rounds.
